overview: This paper systematically studies the optimal clipping bound and batch size for differentially private (DP) deep transfer learning, proposing a theoretical MSE-based optimal clipping bound and a cumulative noise heuristic for batch size selection under fixed-epoch compute budgets.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration Manager
modules.description: Manages the configuration of datasets, models, privacy budgets, and the structured hyperparameter grid search spaces for clipping bound, batch size, and learning rate.

modules.name: Dataset & Poisson DataLoader
modules.description: Implements data loading and preprocessing for image (SUN397, Cassava, CIFAR-100) and text (20 Newsgroups) datasets, utilizing Poisson sampling to enable subsampling-based DP accounting.

modules.name: Model Architecture & PEFT Integration
modules.description: Constructs the backbone models (ViT, DistilBERT, WideResNet) and integrates Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods such as FiLM and LoRA, including specific initialization logic like zero-init for classifier heads.

modules.name: DP Gradient Modifier
modules.description: Implements per-sample gradient computation, per-example clipping (both normalized and unnormalized variants), and the injection of calibrated Gaussian noise to ensure differential privacy.

modules.name: Privacy Accountant
modules.description: Implements the Privacy Random Variable (PRV) accountant to compute the required noise multiplier based on the target privacy budget, sampling rate, and number of training steps.

modules.name: DP Optimizer Integration
modules.description: Wraps the DP gradient modification logic with standard optimizers (Adam, SGD) to create the complete differentially private optimization step, handling the decoupling of learning rate and clipping bound.

modules.name: Theoretical MSE & Clipping Analyzer
modules.description: Implements the mathematical derivations from the paper, including the MSE decomposition (clipping bias vs. noise variance), the optimal clipping bound calculation (Theorem 5.2), and the optimization progress bound (Theorem 5.4).

modules.name: Gradient Re-weighting Analyzer
modules.description: Computes the 'retained weight' metric for classes and samples to quantify how clipping acts as gradient re-weighting, down-weighting hard examples/classes and shifting the optimization signal.

modules.name: Automatic Clipping Baseline (AUTO-S)
modules.description: Implements the Automatic Clipping (AUTO-S) baseline method for comparison, which normalizes each per-sample gradient individually, effectively simulating a very small clipping bound.

modules.name: Fixed-Epoch Training Loop
modules.description: Orchestrates the training process under a fixed-epoch compute budget, managing the iteration steps, calling the DP optimizer, and logging training dynamics and intermediate metrics.

modules.name: Gradient Norm Statistics Tracker
modules.description: Hooks into the training loop to capture and log the distribution of per-sample gradient norms across epochs and classes, enabling the analysis of how difficulty affects gradient norms.

modules.name: Batch Size & Cumulative Noise Analyzer
modules.description: Calculates the cumulative DP noise over the training duration for different batch sizes under fixed epochs, analyzing the trade-off between the number of steps and noise variance to determine optimal batch size.

modules.name: Evaluation Pipeline
modules.description: Evaluates the trained models on test sets, computing macro accuracy and per-class accuracy to assess performance across different levels of learning problem difficulty.

modules.name: Visualization & Reporting
modules.description: Generates the paper's specific visualizations, including accuracy heatmaps over hyperparameter grids, gradient norm violin plots, retained weight curves, and cumulative noise vs. batch size curves.
